facts.fact: The EU action document says GovNet, the government network, has over the years connected about 1,000 public institutions and organs at central level and across 141 districts, but that underinvestment in middle- and last-mile infrastructure leaves many local administrations insufficiently connected; no date is given, so the document's published date is used.

The EU action document gives GovNet's reach as about 1,000 public institutions across the central level and 141 districts and says many local administrations remain insufficiently connected, with no count or share of local administrations on the network; no date is given, so the document's published date is used.

The EU action document says local administrations, with schools, health and justice facilities, are still hardly providing digital public services, so citizens rely on in-person procedures; no date is given, so the document's published date is used.

The Team Europe action that expands GovNet in selected districts has a total estimated cost of EUR 7.1 million, of which EUR 5 million is the EU budget contribution, under the 2026 annual action plan for Mozambique; dated by the document's published date.

The EU's costed 2026 action (EUR 7.1 million) plans to expand GovNet in selected districts to strengthen secure connectivity for public institutions, in support of the national Internet for All 2030 strategy and after stating that many local administrations are insufficiently connected; dated by the document's published date.

The EU action document describes GovNet as the government's own network and names INAGE, the national e-government institute, as managing e-government platforms and data centres; dated by the document's published date.

The EU's annual action plan for Mozambique for 2026 carries a EUR 7.1 million Team Europe action to expand GovNet in selected districts; the date is the document's published date, itself taken from the file's reference number.
